newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bomb wrecks Peruvian store in southwest Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Bomb wrecks Peruvian store in southwest Colombia.

text.p: A bomb wrecked a Peruvian-owned supermarket and damaged at least 30 other shops when it exploded in the southwest Colombian city of Cali early on Christmas Day, police said.
Nobody was hurt in the blast but the store, part of the Peruvian Carsa supermarket chain, was severely damaged and windows were blown out of nearby buildings.
A police spokesman said the bomb consisted of at least 22 pounds (10 kg) of dynamite and was thrown from the window of a taxi about 2 a.m. (0700 GMT).

The motive for the attack was not immediately clear. Police were unable to say whether it may be linked in some way to the takeover of the Japanese embassy residence in Lima by Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels more than a week ago.

Cali was one of the focal points for a joint guerrilla battalion formed by Colombia's M-19, MRTA and Ecuador's Alfaro Vive Carajo! in the mid-1980s. At least 50 high-ranking members of the MRTA, which had only recently been formed, trained in the area under the guidance of the more experienced Colombian rebels.

The bomb was the fourth major blast in 10 days in Colombia. One woman died and 48 were injured in an explosion in Medellin while four people died and scores more were hurt when a bomb went off in the northwest city of Monteria. A third bomb in Bogota virtually destroyed the headquarters of the Communist Party newspaper but caused no injuries.
